clue.text: Drop ecstasy in trance

indicators.note: in tells us the ecstasy abbreviation goes inside the word for a drop of drink

parts.note: a dram is a small drop of spirits
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drug and drifts off into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamy state of absorption is a kind of trance, a waking reverie.

clue.text: Wannabe star — pain to manage

indicators.note: to manage something is to sort it out, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being a would-be celebrity is painful to cope with.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aspiring to a position or fame, the hopeful who wants to be something, is a would-be.

clue.text: Stew's thick — tasteless!

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble cooked together, so the letters that follow are mixed up

parts.note: the S attached to Stew is taken as a letter in its own right

explanation.surface: A cook's thick stew is condemned as lacking any flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' is the anagram signal; the S of its 's joins THICK to make the fodder STHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch art is vulgar and showy, lacking good taste; a culinary sense of tasteless misleads here.

clue.text: Little room in the local to get tight

definitions.meaning: a small cosy bar room in a British pub, the local

explanation.surface: Drinkers head for the small pub room to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests drunkenness in the surface; here it means close-fitting. The local is a British neighbourhood pub, and a snug its small private bar room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy small bar parlour in a pub has this name; a closely fitting garment is likewise described.

clue.text: Show up the French at any time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: French visitors could turn up whenever they like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LA + EVER as a whole, giving REVE + AL.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose or display something is to show it.

clue.text: It's a bad habit to use advertisement's choice of words

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement
diction is a speaker's choice and use of words

explanation.surface: Copywriters' fondness for certain wording is seen as a vice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependency or compulsion one cannot stop is a harmful habit.

clue.text: Prophetic spectre in play

indicators.note: the letters are played with, moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A ghost in a drama foretells the future, as Hamlet's father does.
explanation.definitionFit: Having foreknowledge of events is being prophetic.

clue.text: Is desperate for massages, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: kneads means massages, working the muscles

explanation.surface: Someone stiff and sore is longing for a rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To require something badly is to be desperate for it.

clue.text: Pontoon — a card game

definitions.meaning: a pontoon is a floating structure that can span water
a card game for four players in partnerships

explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is itself a card game, which tempts you to read both halves as one; here it is the floating crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon is a temporary river crossing, and the partnership game of tricks and bidding shares the name.

clue.text: Trouble on Hampstead heath for east enders?

definitions.text: Trouble on Hampstead heath for east enders?

parts.words: Trouble on Hampstead heath for east enders?
parts.note: Hampstead Heath is rhyming slang for teeth among Cockneys, so the trouble is a dental one

explanation.surface: Residents of East London have a problem on a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampstead Heath is a park in north London; in Cockney rhyming slang, used by East Enders, it means teeth. Trouble with teeth is decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental decay is the trouble that affects teeth.

clue.text: Plant — where one may find it flipping excellent

parts.note: a garden is where the plant would be found

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word for excellent is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, excellent, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a superb spot for growing a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive; it reverses AI (A1, excellent) to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardenia is a fragrant white-flowered evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Cinders, after midnight, splits

indicators.note: after places the remains of the fire behind the middle letter

parts.note: the middle of the word night is G
cinders are ashes

explanation.surface: Cinderella's gown tears apart when the clock strikes twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinders evokes Cinderella at midnight, but here it means ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashes are deep cuts or rents, as splits in a surface are.

clue.text: Old dancer missing first and last steps

definitions.note: plural in the clue; one stair is a single step, and the flight is the steps

indicators.note: the dancer's name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Fred Astaire was a famous dancer of old Hollywood films

explanation.surface: An elderly dancer trips on the top and bottom steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a staircase, so the word stands for steps in a flight.

clue.text: Thin copper instrument

parts.note: a copper is a police officer, here a DI, detective inspector
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A slender metal musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like the metal; it is British slang for a police officer, here a DI (detective inspector).
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute is to weaken or make thinner by adding water.

clue.text: Gives out Oscar with limp shake

indicators.note: shaking the letters jumbles them into a new order

explanation.surface: An award winner with a weak handshake hands out prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce or declare publicly is to give something out.

clue.text: Not just a little Englander

parts.note: a short informal word for any native of the United Kingdom, not only an English person

explanation.walkthrough: A Little Englander is a narrow-minded English nationalist; read differently, the clue wants a short word for a Briton who may be Scottish or Welsh as much as English.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal short form for a British person covers the Scots and Welsh as well as the English.

clue.text: Find source of ancestry following start of tree

indicators.note: following puts the ancestry word after the first letter
start of picks the opening letter of the word tree

parts.note: race means lineage, ancestry

explanation.surface: A genealogist tracks down family origins starting with a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track it back and discover where it came from.

clue.text: Shake in abject remorse

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie within the words abject remorse

explanation.surface: Someone trembles with abject guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a quiver or trembling, a shake.

clue.text: Experts are very big on public relations

indicators.note: on places the size abbreviation after the other piece in the across answer

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Specialists consider public relations hugely important.
explanation.definitionFit: Professionals are skilled people, experts in their field.

clue.text: Double Dutch, perhaps?

parts.note: Dutch is old Cockney slang for a wife, so two of them at once

explanation.walkthrough: Double Dutch means gibberish; but 'Dutch' (from duchess) is Cockney slang for a wife, so a double wife is having two spouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more than one spouse at once is having a doubled marriage.

clue.text: Crushed capers for jam

indicators.note: crushed means squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Squashed pickled buds for a preserve.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam looks like a preserve; it means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, a jam to be got out of.

clue.text: Cultivated, talented artist's imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside, so the artist goes within the word for talented

parts.note: able means talented
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A gifted painter has been locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is fit for ploughing and growing crops, cultivated.

clue.text: Politician consumed by law and disorder

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside, so the politician goes within the word for law

parts.note: a rule is a law
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP is caught up in a law-and-order debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' is a verb here: to mess up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumple is to crumple or tousle, messing up something neat.

clue.text: Moving some distance taking in outside broadcast

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mile is some distance

explanation.surface: A TV crew travels a long way for a location report.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile means able to move, in motion.

clue.text: Ray's a gent, thank you very much!

definitions.note: Ray's is read as 'Ray is', so the answer follows

parts.note: a gent, gentleman, is a man
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray is thanked for being a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a man's name; it is the fish. TA is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A manta is a very large tropical ray fish with wing-like fins.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing slob — a cove's back inside

indicators.note: inside puts the a-plus-cove piece within the word for slob

parts.note: a lout is a slob, an oaf

indicators.note: back means the inlet word is read backwards

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

explanation.surface: A lazy slob's oaf of a mate returns indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' tempts as British slang for a chap; here it is a small inlet. 'back' reverses only that word, and 'inside' splits the slob word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle loafer who does no work is a worthless good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Gallery opening ten at the earliest

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A museum opens its doors at ten at the earliest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries in London and elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate in London is a famous art museum.

clue.text: Scrounger's urge to enter pub

definitions.note: read as 'Scrounger is', so the answer follows

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the urge word goes into the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A freeloader wants to go into the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar asks others for money, as a scrounger does.

clue.text: Fish was a bit off

definitions.meaning: gave off a bad odour, past tense of to smell

explanation.walkthrough: 'was a bit off' reads as going bad; it means stank.
explanation.definitionFit: A smelt is a small edible fish, and in British spelling it is also the past tense of to smell, as of something gone off.

clue.text: It's impasse, old chum

parts.note: stale means old, no longer fresh
mate is British slang for a chum, a friend

explanation.surface: A deadlock with an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a deadlock where no progress is possible, an impasse.
